claims.claim: For p not dividing the base b, collision detection is exactly repeated-state detection on mismatch-only normalized prefix sums. Moreover, every collision has a witness containing at most p mismatching aligned positions, although its length may exceed p.
claims.evidence: Because b is invertible modulo p, b^e(A_d(e)-A_d(r)) equals F(r,e-r)-F(r+d,e-r). States change only at literal mismatches, including possibly by zero when unequal symbols are congruent modulo p. Thus two retained states repeat exactly when the intervening aligned substrings are unequal and hash equally. Among p+1 retained states a repetition is forced, yielding an existential witness with at most p intervening mismatches.
claims.witness: For retained states B_a=B_c with a<c, take r=0 when a=0 and r=q_a+1 otherwise, and e=q_c+1. The resulting collision contains exactly c-a mismatches. Pigeonhole gives c-a<=p.
claims.search_method: Independent algebraic derivation followed by exhaustive comparison with literal substring collisions on 26,712 small invertible-base strings; no web or external material used.

claims.claim: For p not dividing b, every collision-free input satisfies m_d<=p-1 at every displacement and M<=C(n,p):=sum_{d=1}^{n-1}min(n-d,p-1). Thus M>C(n,p) forces a collision, where C(n,p)=(p-1)(n-p/2) for p<=n and C(n,p)=n(n-1)/2 for p>=n.
claims.evidence: If m_d>=p, the first p+1 retained states force a collision, so collision-freeness implies m_d<=min(n-d,p-1). Each unequal unordered position pair contributes to exactly one displacement, hence M=sum_d m_d. Summing the pointwise bound gives C. Direct evaluation of the sum gives the two stated closed forms.
claims.witness: At the strict boundary, n=3, p=2, b=3, S=001 has M=C=2 and no collision, confirming that only M>C forces a collision.
claims.search_method: Symbolically derived the capacity sum and exhaustively checked the implication, M identity, closed form, and boundary example using exact arithmetic.

claims.claim: In the word-RAM model with p=n^{O(1)}, there is an exact deterministic algorithm running in O(n log n+n+min{D,M,n min(n,p)}) time, where D is the number of distinct substring contents and M is the number of unequal unordered character-position pairs. Consequently the requested O(n log n) bound holds when p=O(log n), D=O(n log n), or M=O(n log n).
claims.evidence: Exact LCE queries enumerate at most min(m_d,p) mismatches per displacement. Including one initial state per displacement gives Q<=n+sum_d min(m_d,p)<=n+min{M,n min(n,p)} records. Sorting word-sized (d,state) keys detects precisely the repetitions from claim 0. Independently, expanding every compact-suffix-tree edge character by character visits each distinct substring content once, in O(D), and sorting (length,fingerprint) detects exactly unequal-content collisions. D and M are computable during O(n log n) preprocessing, so selecting the cheaper route proves the minimum bound. For p dividing b, claim 5 supplies an O(n log n) case algorithm, also within this bound.
claims.witness: The two route sizes are O(n+min{M,n min(n,p)}) and O(n+D); taking their minimum after common O(n log n) preprocessing yields the claimed expression.
claims.search_method: Re-derived record counts, exactness, radix-sort key bounds, distinct-content enumeration, and the case split; exhaustively compared both logical detection routes with literal collision search on small inputs.

claims.claim: There is an infinite family of collision-free invertible-base instances with p=Theta(n), alphabet size at most n, D=Theta(n^2), M=Theta(n^2), and Theta(n^2) retained mismatch states. Hence both audited enumerative routes can require quadratic work even on valid NO instances; this is not a lower bound against arbitrary algorithms.
claims.evidence: For n=p-2 and primitive-root base b, equal-length contents in 0^a1^c are parameterized by their trailing-one count k and hash to G_k. Equality G_k=G_l would imply b^{|k-l|}=1, impossible for 0<|k-l|<=n<p-1=ord_p(b). Counts are D=n+ac, M=ac, and retained states M+n-1; with balanced a,c, all are quadratic where asserted. The conclusion is explicitly limited to the two enumerative routes.
claims.witness: For p=11, n=9, b=2, and S=000011111, b has order 10, the instance is collision-free, M=20, D=29, and the mismatch route retains 28 states. The same formulas apply for every prime p>=5.
claims.search_method: Proved the construction from multiplicative order and exact combinatorial counts, then checked 12 prime instances from p=5 through p=43.

claims.claim: In the word-RAM model with p=n^{O(1)} and p not dividing b, every string with at most two runs has an exact O(n)-time collision test. For S=x^a y^c with x!=y and R=min(a,c), either x=y mod p gives a length-one collision, or a collision exists exactly when G_t:=1+b+...+b^{t-1}=0 mod p for some 1<=t<=R.
claims.evidence: For fixed length L, all distinct contents are x^{L-k}y^k over one interval K_L and have fingerprint xG_L+(y-x)G_k. If x and y are not congruent modulo p, the difference for k<l is (y-x)b^kG_{l-k}, which vanishes exactly when G_{l-k}=0. Every K_L has width at most R. Conversely, t<=R ensures both x^t and y^t occur and collide when G_t=0. Iterating G_{t+1}=bG_t+1 takes O(R)<=O(n) word operations.
claims.witness: The factorization fingerprint(l)-fingerprint(k)=(y-x)b^kG_{l-k} establishes both necessity and, using the two pure-run substrings, sufficiency.
claims.search_method: Independent factorization and interval-width proof, plus exhaustive exact checking of 16,050 two-run instances, including distinct symbols congruent modulo p.

claims.claim: The target has a complete O(n log n) exact solution in the noninvertible case p divides b.
claims.evidence: When p divides b, every nonempty most-significant-first fingerprint equals its final character modulo p. For endpoints e<f in the same residue group, all corresponding equal-length substrings avoid a collision exactly when the reversed prefix R_e is a prefix of R_f. Otherwise their reversed LCP length t<e+1 yields unequal colliding substrings of length t+1. Checking consecutive endpoints suffices by transitivity of the prefix relation. Exact suffix-array/LCP/RMQ preprocessing and residue grouping fit O(n log n).
claims.witness: A failed prefix test R_e not prefix R_f directly returns the two length-(t+1) substrings ending at e and f, where t=LCP(R_e,R_f); both hashes equal their congruent final characters.
claims.search_method: Re-derived the endpoint characterization and transitivity reduction, then exhaustively compared it with literal collision search on 20,449 small noninvertible-base strings.

claims.claim: Collisions cannot occur at length L when b^L<=p, but checking only power-of-two lengths, only lexicographically adjacent contents, or relying on monotonicity in the length is insufficient.
claims.evidence: Distinct canonical length-L base-b words are distinct integers in [0,b^L-1]. If b^L<=p, their nonzero difference has magnitude below p and cannot vanish modulo p. For b=2, p=5, S=000101, literal enumeration confirms that unequal-content collisions occur only at length 3, between values 0 and 5; lengths 1, 2, and 4 are collision-free, and values 1 and 2 lie lexicographically between the colliding contents.
claims.witness: The exact fingerprint arrays are [[0,0,0,1,0,1],[0,0,1,2,1],[0,1,2,0],[1,2,0],[2,0],[0]], with collision-length set exactly {3}.
claims.search_method: Proved the integer-range injectivity bound and reproduced all fingerprint arrays, collision lengths, and lexicographic values using exact arithmetic.

target_evidence: The source requests an O(n log n) or linear collision detector for an arbitrary string and prime, with a permitted small false-rejection probability. The draft proves exact algorithms for the noninvertible case, several adaptive regimes, and at-most-two-run strings, together with valid structural bounds and limitations. It expressly leaves the unrestricted invertible-base case unresolved and claims only PARTIAL resolution. Thus it supplies material correct progress but not a complete proof of the entire target.
